common_name: Mammoth French White Sunchoke (Large White-Skinned Heirloom Jerusalem Artichoke)

planting.note: Plant whole or cut tuber sections, each with at least one or two eyes, 3-5 inches deep around the last frost date in loose, well-drained soil; Mammoth French White is an old heirloom strain selected for unusually large, pale tan-to-white tubers and needs a full season to bulk up fully before frost.

directions: Plant tuber sections 3-5 inches deep in a dedicated, well-drained bed, since sunchokes spread aggressively from any tuber left in the ground and this vigorous heirloom is difficult to fully eradicate once established. Mammoth French White is an old French-derived heirloom strain valued for producing notably large, pale tan-to-white tubers substantially bigger than wild-type or unnamed sunchoke stock, which means fewer tubers are needed to fill a basket and less scrubbing per pound at harvest, though the tubers still carry some of the knobbiness typical of the species rather than the smooth club shape of Fuseau-type strains. Plants grow tall and coarse, 6-9 feet, topped with small yellow sunflowers in late summer before dying back with frost; tubers are ready to dig once tops are killed and can be harvested through winter into early spring as needed. A light frost is said to sweeten the flavor by converting stored inulin into simple sugars. Leave a portion of tubers in the ground each year to regenerate next season's crop, and rotate or contain the bed to keep the planting from spreading into unwanted areas.
sources: University of Minnesota Extension — Jerusalem Artichoke
